prd.name: Design
prd.overview: The shared design system for BedTerm's app chrome — colour tokens, the shipped app icon, and the system-appearance rules that bind both to iOS Light / Dark mode. Each requirement below is a self-contained slice of the design system referenced by the feature PRDs.

requirement.name: Colour Tokens

description.p: Every user-visible app-chrome surface, text, icon, border, and accent colour resolves to one of the named tokens below. Each token has both a Light value and a Dark value; SwiftUI/UIKit resolve them automatically as the iOS system appearance changes. Tokens are referenced by semantic name (e.g. surface.elevated) — never by palette name. The terminal viewport's own palette is tracked separately under R3 — System Appearance and is currently deferred.

tr.td: Root screen background behind every view.
Tint colour, Send button, active CTRL fill, onboarding glyph.
Text/glyphs that sit on top of an accent fill.
Inline error text, host-key mismatch warnings, disconnect banner.
Tint layered over the Liquid Glass material on the R3 capsule and compose pill.

requirement.rule: The catalogue defines exactly these eight tokens: surface.background, surface.elevated, text.primary, text.muted, accent, accent.label, error, keybar.background.
Every token has both a Light value and a Dark value. Switching system appearance resolves each token to its Dark or Light variant automatically.
Tokens use semantic names that describe their role (surface.elevated, text.muted) — not palette names (gray800, blue500).

No literal colour values appear in code or views: no Color(red:green:blue:), no UIColor(red:green:blue:), no hex strings, no Color.black / .white / .gray / other static Color.<name> constants on user-visible surfaces.

Adaptive SwiftUI symbolic colours — Color.primary, Color.secondary, Color.accentColor, .tint, materials such as .regularMaterial — are acceptable. They are already system-adaptive and do not need a custom token.

requirement.name: App Icon

description.p: BedTerm ships with a final designed app icon — not the Xcode placeholder — so it has a recognisable identity on the Home Screen, in Spotlight, in Settings, and in the App Switcher. The shipped icon set covers every iOS-required size and every Home Screen appearance mode introduced in iOS 18: Light, Dark, and Tinted.

requirement.rule: A final app icon design exists and is shipped at all iOS-required sizes (Home Screen, Spotlight, Settings, Notifications, App Store marketing).
The icon ships variants for iOS 18+ Dark and Tinted Home Screen appearances in addition to the default Light variant.

requirement.name: System Appearance

description.p: The app always follows the iOS system appearance — Light when the system is Light, Dark when the system is Dark — for both the SwiftUI chrome and the terminal palette. There is no in-app theme override.

The colour tokens that back this behaviour are defined under R1 — Colour Tokens. App-chrome rules below are implemented against those tokens; the terminal palette rules remain deferred until the Metal renderer's ANSI colour map is bridged through the same tokens.

requirement.rule: On launch, the app chrome renders in Light or Dark to match the current iOS system appearance, without any in-app theme picker.
Changing the system appearance while the app is open updates the app chrome without restart.
When the system is in Light mode, the terminal uses a light background with dark foreground text and legible ANSI colour mappings.
When the system is in Dark mode, the terminal uses a dark background with light foreground text and legible ANSI colour mappings.
In both appearances, the special-keys bar, Connect form, error text, and disconnect banner meet contrast standards against their background.

Every app-chrome surface, text, icon, border, and accent colour is sourced from a design-system token in the catalogue with both Light and Dark variants — no literal colour values in code. Switching system appearance changes the rendered colour of every coloured element.

bug.current: The project has no AppIcon asset — the app launches with the default white/blank iOS placeholder icon on the Home Screen, in Spotlight, and in the App Switcher. No icon design has been produced yet.
bug.expected: A final app icon design is produced and added as an AppIcon asset catalog entry covering every iOS-required size, including Dark and Tinted variants for iOS 18+.
bug.steps: 1. Build and install the app on a device or simulator. 2. Go to the Home Screen. 3. Observe: the app appears with the generic placeholder icon instead of a designed icon.

bug.current: The app forces Dark appearance at the root, so it renders dark even when the iOS system is in Light mode. The terminal also stays on a dark palette regardless of system setting.
bug.expected: The app and terminal mirror the iOS system appearance — Light in Light, Dark in Dark — with no in-app override. Toggling system appearance while the app is open swaps both the SwiftUI chrome and the terminal palette live.
bug.steps: 1. Set the iOS system appearance to Light (Settings → Display & Brightness → Light). 2. Launch the app. 3. Observe: the app and terminal render in Dark instead of Light. 4. With the app open, switch the system appearance to Dark and back to Light. 5. Observe: the app does not react to the system change.
